Confirmed by compiling:
- 01: a :root variable makes no bg-brand utility.
- 04: --font-editor: 700 still gives font-family.

- 07: --color-*: initial also removes bg-white and bg-black, while bg-transparent and text-current stay.
- 08: --*: initial keeps flex.
- 09: inline gives font-family: var(--font-inter).

- 12: matches the docs' sharing-across-projects section.

Not flagged, but worth a look:

- sr2-05 reuses the docs' own --font-script example.

Prompt rules: the v4.3 baseline is correct. The upgrade-guide trap is real: the guide contains --text-red-500 (2 matches) as well as --color-red-500. verdicts.notes:
I read the prompt (DECK, SECTIONS, source step, RULES, level rules) and fetched the raw HTML of https://tailwindcss.com/docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files and https://tailwindcss.com/docs/functions-and-directives on 2026-10-13. The docs header still shows 4.3, so the prompt's v4 / v4.3 baseline is correct.

Prompt rules checked and found correct:
- Tailwind scans source files as plain text.
- Complete class names are detected; constructed fragments are not.
- Automatic scanning excludes node_modules, .gitignore'd files, binary files, CSS files and lock files.
- @source paths are stylesheet-relative.
- Automatic detection starts at the current working directory by default.
- source("../src") sets the detection base.
- source(none) disables automatic detection.
- @source not ignores paths.
- @source inline() safelists classes; variants need {hover:,focus:,}; the input is brace expanded.
- @source not inline() excludes classes.
- functions-and-directives says \"To safelist utilities in v4 use @source inline()\".
I found no prompt rule for this section to be wrong.

Cards that pass: 01, 02, 04, 05, 08, 10, 11, 12.
- 11: hover:underline needs an explicit {hover:,} prefix; the docs confirm this.
- 12: the docs say \"The source input is brace expanded\" and show bg-red-{50,{100..900..100},950}.

Possible nuance, not flagged: the docs say automatic detection starts at the current working directory. Individual integrations (for example the Vite plugin) may pass their own base. I did not verify this, and the docs' wording supports the cards as written.

Not flagged, but should be fixed: every r3 explanation is 25 to 70 characters and mostly restates the statement. verdicts.notes:
I checked all 12 r4 cards. I downloaded the hover-focus-and-other-states, dark-mode and upgrade-guide pages directly. Both docs pages show 'Tailwind CSS v4.3' in their header, so the prompt's v4 / v4.3 pin is correct. The r4 rules in the prompt also hold on the official pages: v4 hover: compiles to @media (hover: hover) { &:hover } (quick reference plus the upgrade guide's 'Hover styles on mobile' section); default dark uses prefers-color-scheme; a @custom-variant dark selector override replaces the media query; the data-theme example is &:where([data-theme=dark], [data-theme=dark] *); and the docs say theme persistence (localStorage, server side) is 'totally up to you'. I found no prompt rule wrong for this section.

Passing cards, with minor observations:
- sr4-02 is correct. Its source is the upgrade guide, which describes the v4.0 change. The current states page quick reference ('hover @media (hover: hover) { &:hover }') is a better current-behavior URL; optional swap.
- sr4-04 (focus-within) is partly guessable from the word 'within'. I did not flag it, but it is borderline.
- sr4-07 (checked: means live :checked, not the [checked] attribute) and sr4-11 (the data-theme selector also matches the marked element) are correct. Both lean on CSS/HTML selector semantics that css-fundamentals owns. Acceptable because the Tailwind-generated selector decides the answer.
- sr4-08 is correct (stacked focus:invalid: requires both conditions; the docs example uses focus:invalid:border-pink-500). Difficulty 3 is overstated; 2 fits.
- sr4-09, sr4-10 and sr4-12 are verified against the dark-mode page.

Section balance: the four replacements keep 6 true / 6 false (01 F to F, 03 F to F, 05 F to F, 06 T to T). They also break the repeated 'variant does a non-styling job' false template (01, 05, 12), which came from the prompt's 'These variants style existing state' trap.

Explanation: "Unnamed group-* variants compile to a descendant selector of any .group ancestor, so hovering an outer group also triggers them. If you know one card you know the other, so it is a mirrored pair. Its "preceding peer" wording also repeats sr5-03's sibling-order fact. Implicit groups (in-*), a relational variant on the same page, is not tested anywhere.

verdicts.notes:
The source page loaded (HTTP 200): https://tailwindcss.com/docs/hover-focus-and-other-states. Its static HTML contains ">4.3<", which fits the prompt's v4.3 baseline. All 12 r5 cards use this page. They passed source and factual checks; none has a wrong answer.

Cards that passed:
- sr5-01 (group-focus): generated as :where(.group):focus *.
- sr5-03 (peer): \"the peer marker can only be used on previous siblings\".
- sr5-05 (has-checked): \"Use the has-* variant to style an element based on the state or content of its descendants\".
- sr5-06 (group-has): searches the group's descendants.

Prompt rules I found wrong or overstated:
1. The r11 scope and the tooling rule present "automatic vendor prefixing and nesting processing" as unconditional. In the source, the Lightning CSS pass (nesting flattening plus prefixing for Safari 16.4, Chrome 111 and Firefox 128) runs only in optimized builds: Vite build (not the dev server), PostCSS when NODE_ENV is production or optimize is set, and the CLI with --minify or --optimize. The docs' wording hides this. Cards on these features must name the optimized build.
2. The stale-material rule says "@tailwind directives ... were removed". That is too absolute. The v4 package's own utilities.css is literally "@tailwind utilities;", and index.css imports it, so the directive still exists inside v4. The user-facing entry is @import "tailwindcss", as the upgrade guide says. No r11 card depends on this.

The other r11 prompt rules match the live v4.3 docs: @reference for separately processed styles, referencing the main stylesheet in customized projects, Sass/Less/Stylus not designed to work with v4, and subpath imports for @import, @reference, @plugin and @config.

scan.tells:
Lengths are balanced. Statement length averages 80.5 characters on True cards and 80.6 on False cards, and every section is within 5 characters (largest gaps: r7 +4.8, r5 -4.3, r10 +4.0). Explanations average 64 (True) against 65 (False). Hedge words are balanced: 'can' 7 True / 6 False, 'automatically' 2/2. The exploitable tells are wording and templates.

1. Narrowing or limiting verbs are always False (5/5): restricts (sr3-01, sr5-06), confines (sr7-04), limits (sr2-03), waits for (sr5-10). This recurring 'X restricts/limits Y' template carries more than the allowed 2 false statements.

2. 'Tailwind treats X as ...' is always False (3/3): sr6-04, sr7-11, sr8-07. It is a recurring mislabel template.

3. Over-reaching side-effect verbs appear only in False statements: triggers (sr1-06), duplicates (sr1-02), raises (sr1-10), stretches (sr9-09), resets (sr12-09), tracks (sr7-05), keeps (sr6-08), replaces (sr2-05, sr10-07), 'still requires' (sr4-10), 'unsupported' (sr7-11). That makes 11 cards, all False.

4. Verbs that lean True. 'Tailwind accepts' at the start of a statement: 4/4 True (sr7-12, sr8-10, sr9-10, sr10-04); 'accepts' overall is 4 True / 2 False. 'uses': 5/0 True (sr5-09, sr7-02, sr10-01, sr11-01, sr12-08). 'includes': 2/0 True (sr4-02, sr9-02). '... makes X available': 3 True (sr6-06, sr6-12, sr7-09) against 1 False (sr2-09). 'selects' leans False: 3 False (sr7-07, sr9-06, sr9-12) against 1 True (sr7-08).

5. Preflight cards are 6 False / 3 True. When Preflight is the subject and the verb keeps a browser default or picks a value, the card is always False: 'retains/preserves browser margins/numbering' (sr9-04, sr9-07), 'selects text-2xl/content-box' (sr9-06, sr9-12), 'stretches' (sr9-09). The only True ones use 'supplies' or 'changes' (sr9-05, sr9-08).

6. 'honors legacy ... configuration options' is 2/2 False (sr12-03, sr12-12). In r12, every claim that v4 keeps a legacy mechanism is False (sr12-01 auto-discovers, sr12-03, sr12-06 exposes resolveConfig, sr12-12), apart from sr12-04 and sr12-05.

7. 'also' marks over-generalization: 2 of 3 are False (sr3-11 'also generate hover:underline', sr10-09 'also registers -shift-*'; the True one is sr4-11).

8. Name-match tell for variant cards. When the variant name equals the generated pseudo-class, the card is True (sr4-06 invalid:→:invalid, sr4-08 focus:invalid:→:focus+:invalid, sr5-05 has-checked→:has(:checked)). When it does not match, the card is False (sr4-03 focus-visible: shown as :focus). sr4-06 is effectively a name-giveaway card.

9. Variant-performs-an-action template, 2/2 False: sr4-05 (disabled: disables), sr4-12 (dark variant persists to localStorage).

10. Mirrored opening: sr3-10 (True) and sr3-11 (False) both start 'An @source inline('underline') directive can ...'.

11. Truism or giveaway risk: sr8-01 ('can compile responsive variants' of bracket values), sr11-04 (v4 starts with @import 'tailwindcss', installation knowledge), sr11-08 (the Vite plugin compiles Tailwind in Vite). A player answers True from general sense.

12. Difficulty 3 is skewed slightly towards False (10 True / 14 False), so a hard card is a weak signal for False. The appliesTo label 'Tailwind CSS v4.3' (10 cards) does not predict the answer.

edits.sectionBalance: r1: 11 cards, 6T/5F. r2: 9 cards, 4T/5F. r3: 9 cards, 5T/4F. r4: 9 cards, 5T/4F. r5: 9 cards, 4T/5F. r6: 9 cards, 4T/5F. r7: 9 cards, 5T/4F. r8: 9 cards, 5T/4F. r9: 10 cards, 5T/5F. r10: 11 cards, 6T/5F. r11: 9 cards, 5T/4F. r12: 11 cards, 5T/6F. Deck total 115 cards (59T/56F), from 144.
edits.notes:
Method: I downloaded the official v4.3 pages (styling-with-utility-classes, theme, colors, font-family, detecting-classes-in-source-files, hover-focus-and-other-states, dark-mode, responsive-design, adding-custom-styles, preflight, functions-and-directives, compatibility, the Vite/PostCSS/CLI installation pages, upgrade-guide, max-width, play-cdn) and checked every rewrite against them. Nothing was edited, and no git, gh or vercel command was run.

Decisions that depart from a verifier's suggestion:
- sr2-02 dropped, not rewritten. The suggested card (a nested @theme is hoisted globally) rests only on how the 4.3.3 compiler behaves, and the official page says the opposite ("required to be defined top-level").
- sr11-06 rewritten without the verifier's "when it optimizes a build" condition. That condition, and the unoptimized-dev-server behaviour, appear only in the GitHub source, not on tailwindcss.com. I rebuilt the card on the upgrade guide's documented consequence: prefixing is handled for you, so autoprefixer can be removed.
- sr11-07 dropped for the same reason: no clean card could be checked on the docs. To keep r11 at 9 cards, I rewrote sr11-09 with the verifier's Vite-versus-PostCSS replacement. Its explanation keeps only what the Vite page itself says.
- sr9-05: the explanation avoids the docs' stale sentence that "the border class only sets border-width". The verifier's border-style claim comes from the compiler, not the docs, so it is left out too.
- sr3-03: source fix only (see "source"). Statement, answer and explanation are unchanged.

Rewrites to keep sections at size and balance:
- r4: dropping all 5 weak/duplicate cards would leave 7. I rewrote sr4-05 (False) and sr4-06 (True) and dropped sr4-01, sr4-03 and sr4-09. I chose 05 and 06 over the 01 and 03 replacements because those two give away sr4-02 (the hover media condition).
- r5: dropping would leave 7 cards (2T/5F). I rewrote sr5-07 (in-* implicit groups) and sr5-12 (group-aria-*), both True. I chose them over the 04 and 09 replacements as the less guessable cards.

Tell rewrites (5), each keeping its fact and answer:
- Narrowing verbs: sr3-01 (restricts), sr5-06 (restricts), sr7-04 (confines).
- Statement-initial "Tailwind accepts": sr9-10 and sr10-04.
After these and the drops, "restricts/confines/limits" are gone and "Tailwind accepts" survives only in sr7-12 and sr8-10.

Residual items not fixed:
- sr3-10 and sr3-11 still share the opening "An @source inline('underline') directive can"; they are in a conflict group.
- The over-reaching-verb False pattern (duplicates, raises, stretches, resets, tracks, keeps, replaces) is still present in the remaining False cards.
- Optional source upgrades the verifiers suggested, which I did not apply because those cards were not flagged:
  - sr6-11 to /docs/responsive-design#using-arbitrary-values
  - sr8-04 to adding-custom-styles#handling-whitespace
  - sr8-03 to adding-custom-styles#resolving-ambiguities
  - sr4-02 to the states page quick reference
  - sr7-03 to /docs/responsive-design
- Many surviving explanations are very short (under 70 characters) and only restate the verdict, especially in r3, r5 and r7. They are worth an enrichment pass.

Prompt rule issues for the deck definition:
1. r11's "automatic vendor prefixing and nesting processing" is applied unconditionally. In the official source it runs only in optimized builds, and the docs do not say so. Future cards should avoid these as unconditional claims.
2. "Removed container center/padding configuration" holds only for CSS-first configuration, because the v4.3.3 compatibility layer still honors them from an @config JS file.
3. "@theme must be top-level" is documented but not enforced by the compiler.
4. The docs' Preflight claim that "the border class only sets border-width" is stale against v4.3 output.
5. "@tailwind directives were removed" is too absolute: they are still used inside the package's own utilities.css.
6. The r5 scope leaves out the in-* and group-aria-*/peer-aria-* variants, which are documented, good material (now used in sr5-07 and sr5-12).

cards.statement: Tailwind generates CSS for the utility classes it finds in your project when you compile your CSS.
cards.explanation: Tailwind isn't one big prebuilt stylesheet: it builds just the styles your classes need at compile time, which is how a one-off class like bg-[#316ff6] works.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. Confirmed on styling-with-utility-classes: 'isn't one big static stylesheet ... generates the CSS needed based on the classes you're actually using when you compile your CSS', with the bg-[#316ff6] example.

cards.statement: Tailwind finds utility candidates by parsing the class attributes in your HTML templates.
cards.explanation: Tailwind treats every source file as plain text and picks out class-like tokens wherever they appear, without parsing the file as code.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. Confirmed on detecting-classes-in-source-files: 'treats all of your source files as plain text, and doesn't attempt to actually parse your files as code'.

cards.statement: Tailwind's disabled: variant matches a button that signals its state with aria-disabled="true" alone.
cards.explanation: disabled: compiles to :disabled, which needs the native disabled state; a button marked only with aria-disabled="true" needs Tailwind's aria-disabled: variant.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. Confirmed in the states page quick reference ('disabled &:disabled') and the ARIA table ('aria-disabled &[aria-disabled="true"]').

cards.statement: Tailwind's invalid: styles show on an empty required field before the user has typed anything.
cards.explanation: invalid: compiles to :invalid, which matches as soon as the value fails validation; Tailwind's user-invalid: variant waits until the user has interacted with the field.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. Confirmed on the states page: 'invalid &:invalid', 'user-invalid &:user-invalid', and 'Style an input when it's invalid and the user has interacted with it, using the user-invalid variant'.

cards.statement: Tailwind's group-has-[a]: looks for a link inside the styled element's own subtree.
cards.explanation: group-has-[a]: runs its :has() check on the element marked group, so the link can sit anywhere inside that group.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. Confirmed on the states page: 'mark the parent with the group class and use the group-has-* variant'. In the example the svg uses group-has-[a]:block and the link is elsewhere in the group.

cards.statement: Tailwind's in-focus: variant reacts to focus on any parent element, whether or not that parent has the group class.
cards.explanation: The in-* variants respond to a state change in any ancestor and need no marker class, so in-focus: also fires when an outer wrapper higher up receives focus.
cards.reason: Applied the wording lens fix: the old explanation said group-* needs a group marker, which is the answer to sr5-01. Confirmed under 'Implicit groups': 'you don't need to add group to the parent element' and 'The in-* variant responds to state changes in any parent'.

cards.statement: Tailwind's group-aria-[sort=ascending]: checks aria-sort on the group ancestor rather than on the styled element.
cards.explanation: Tailwind compiles it to :where(.group)[aria-sort="ascending"] *, so an icon inside a th marked group rotates once that th is sorted ascending.
cards.reason: The wording lens's drop holds up. The card tests the same principle as sr5-01 and sr5-06, that a group-* variant checks its condition on the group ancestor, so knowing either one answers this card. The fact lens also found the explanation wrong: in the docs example ascending applies rotate-0 (0deg) and only descending applies rotate-180. Fixing it would still leave the duplicate, so the card is dropped.

cards.statement: Tailwind's @sm: variant stops matching once its container reaches the @md size.
cards.explanation: Tailwind compiles @sm: to @container (width >= 24rem), a minimum with no upper bound, so its styles stay active as the container grows past @md.
cards.reason: Both lenses fix the explanation: 'mobile-first like breakpoints' gave away sr6-02. Merged into one version based on the generated query only. Confirmed in the responsive-design table ('@sm 24rem ... @container (width >= 24rem)') and in 'apply at the target container size and up'.

cards.statement: Preflight's border reset strips the browser-drawn borders from text inputs and buttons.
cards.explanation: Preflight applies border: 0 solid to every element plus ::before, ::after, ::backdrop and ::file-selector-button, which overrides the user-agent borders on text inputs and buttons.
cards.reason: Applied the fact lens fix. 'All elements' plus 'inputs' was too broad: checkbox and radio inputs keep their native drawing, and the explanation's 'every pseudo-element' overstated the selector list. Confirmed in Preflight 'Border styles are reset': '*, ::after, ::before, ::backdrop, ::file-selector-button { box-sizing: border-box; border: 0 solid; }' for all elements.

cards.statement: Tailwind's docs put a project's own element defaults, such as h1 styles, in @layer base rather than @layer components.
cards.explanation: Element defaults belong in Tailwind's base layer, for example @layer base { h1 { color: red; } }; the docs keep @layer components for class-based components like .card.
cards.reason: Merged both fixes. The statement uses the wording lens's base-versus-components contrast so it is no longer a truism. The explanation stops attributing the h1 color example to the docs, which use h1/h2 font-size, per the fact lens. I also removed 'Preflight lives in the base layer' because that is sr9-02's answer. Confirmed on adding-custom-styles: base styles for HTML elements go in the base layer, and component classes like .card go in the components layer.

cards.statement: In Tailwind CSS v4, a normal utility beats a conflicting normal @layer components rule with a more specific selector.
cards.explanation: Tailwind orders its utilities layer after components; for declarations without !important a later cascade layer wins whatever the selector specificity.
cards.reason: Applied the wording lens fix: the statement now states importance, because !important reverses layer order and that technicality could be defended against the old wording. I trimmed the full layer list from the explanation so it no longer restates sr9-01. Confirmed on preflight ('@layer theme, base, components, utilities') and adding-custom-styles ('you can still use utility classes to override them').

cards.statement: A nested &::-webkit-scrollbar rule inside @utility styles the scrollbar of the element using that utility.
cards.explanation: Nesting inside @utility adds an extra selector to the generated utility, as in the docs' scrollbar-hidden example.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. Confirmed under adding-custom-styles 'Complex utilities': '@utility scrollbar-hidden { &::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; } }'.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 adds vendor prefixes itself, which makes autoprefixer unnecessary in its PostCSS setup.
cards.explanation: Vendor prefixing is part of Tailwind's own CSS processing in v4, so the upgrade guide removes autoprefixer from the PostCSS plugin list.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. Confirmed in the upgrade guide 'Using PostCSS': 'in v4 imports and vendor prefixing is now handled for you automatically, so you can remove postcss-import and autoprefixer'.

cards.statement: Tailwind's docs name the PostCSS plugin as the most seamless way to add Tailwind to SvelteKit.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's docs call the Vite plugin the most seamless way to integrate with frameworks like Laravel, SvelteKit, React Router, Nuxt and SolidJS.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. Confirmed on installation/using-vite: 'Installing Tailwind CSS as a Vite plugin is the most seamless way to integrate it with frameworks like Laravel, SvelteKit, React Router, Nuxt, and SolidJS.'

cards.statement: In Tailwind CSS v4, --container-* tokens in @theme set the container utility's centering and padding.
cards.explanation: The upgrade guide replaces v3's container center and padding options with CSS: @utility container { margin-inline: auto; padding-inline: 2rem; }.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. Confirmed in the upgrade guide 'Container configuration': the center and padding options 'no longer exist in v4', and the guide shows the @utility container replacement.
